public_comment.topic: Asked the commission's permission for a sewer line easement across his own land off Sunny Hill Drive/West Street to connect a planned four-house common-driveway subdivision to town sewer, citing a recent bylaw change allowing common driveways and a similar project he had built in Ashburnham.

votes.motion: Accept the notice of commitment for FY2026 sewer billing

budget_items.what_was_said: The quarterly bill run went out but took six days due to a software/system upgrade with the billing vendor that caused printing errors, including old 2023 bills reappearing. The issue reportedly affected other municipalities using the same vendor, not just Lunenburg.

budget_items.topic: FY2026 notice of commitment / billing amounts
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission needed to review and sign off on the FY2026 billing commitment amounts and the percentage of past-due accounts; the percent-past-due figure could not be updated until the next demand notice run. A member agreed to stop by the DPW office to sign it.

The commission recalled having discussed a possible flat-rate connection fee for accessory dwelling units of two bedrooms or fewer, with additional-bedroom scaling similar to regular connections, but noted the bylaw currently requires a separate connection to the street for every dwelling.

The commission discussed possibly spending a small amount from its budget on popcorn or cotton candy for the DPW's Touch a Truck/school-supply fundraiser, with one figure mentioned as an upper limit before a commissioner offered to donate his own cotton candy machine instead.

decisions.decision: Ed McWeeny was asked to assemble a full package/presentation, including potential problems avoided by the easement, before bringing the Sunny Hill Drive easement request to a formal hearing.
Two commission members agreed to attend the August 21 Town Council meeting on the ADU sewer bylaw question, since a quorum of the commission itself could not attend.

The commission will accept school-supply donations for the Touch a Truck event at the DPW office, and a commissioner will bring a table and a personal cotton candy machine rather than the commission purchasing supplies.
The manhole repair project is expected to be completed before the first frost, once a subcontractor is scheduled to replace framing and covers.
A formal request for the Sunny Hill Drive easement/extension will require a noticed public hearing, with at least five days' newspaper notice.

minutes.headline: Sewer Commission weighed letting a developer easement across town land for a new subdivision, decided nothing yet
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Sewer Commission heard a developer's request for a sewer-line easement to serve a planned common-driveway subdivision on Sunny Hill Drive, and spent much of the meeting debating the precedent such an easement could set for future development and accessory dwelling units. Members also approved the FY29 minutes and the FY2026 billing commitment, discussed a billing-system glitch, an upcoming Town Council meeting on ADU sewer bylaws, a DPW school-supply fundraiser, and got an update on the manhole repair project, without making any final decision on the easement itself.

what_happened.line: A developer asked the Sewer Commission for an easement across town land to serve a new Sunny Hill Drive subdivision; no decision was made.
The commission asked the developer to prepare a full presentation before bringing the easement to a formal public hearing.
Any formal easement request will need a noticed public hearing with at least five days' newspaper notice.
The commission voted to accept the FY2026 sewer billing commitment.
A billing-vendor software upgrade delayed the first-quarter FY26 bill run and caused old 2023 bills to reprint.

why_it_matters: The easement request touches how much say the town keeps over private development on town-owned land, and how future accessory dwelling units connect to sewer -- residents will get a formal hearing before anything is decided.
